name: Interior
_design: The room over the cistern, and it is two buildings at once: the office of the crew who read the town’s water, and the place everybody sleeps when a week goes bad. The bunks against the east wall are not decoration and neither is the fire.

text: Painted straight onto the boards over the stairhead, in a hand nobody has bettered:
THREE MARKS. A TICK IS ICE. A CROSS IS NOT ICE. NO MARK IS NOT ICE EITHER.
READ THE FLOOR BEFORE YOU STAND ON IT. THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE TRADE.
THE INTAKE LEDGER. One page a day since 1802, and every page is the same four numbers.
DEPTH. FLOW. CUT. SOUND. Column after column of a town measuring its own water.
Somebody has gone under this building every morning for two hundred and twenty years.
The back of the ledger, where the numbers stop and the arguments start.
1849: CHANNELS CUT WIDE TO GET AHEAD OF THE FREEZE. THE TANK TOOK IN AIR.
1850: WE DO NOT GET AHEAD OF IT. WE FIND OUT WHAT IT IS DOING. AGREED, ALL HANDS.
The chalk bench: boxes of it, graded, and a rack of the long-handled markers.
A card: SIX IN THE MORNING, EVERY CELL, EVERY DAY, WHETHER OR NOT IT CHANGED.
Under that: ESPECIALLY WHEN IT HAS NOT CHANGED. THAT IS WHEN PEOPLE STOP LOOKING.
A rack of thaw pots, black with two centuries of use, hung by size.
The smallest would sit in your hands. The largest takes four people to carry.
A tally beside them: POTS ON THE ICE TODAY. The figure is higher than any year listed.
Eight Bond Crests in a case, one for every Hall in Caelora.
The Frost Crest is sixth and it is the only one that is not the same twice:
it is cut from lake ice each winter and the case is a cold box with a lamp in it.
A notice by the street door, hung at the height of a sixteen-year-old:
IF YOU ARE GOING DOWN, TELL THE DESK. IF YOU ARE COMING UP, TELL THE DESK.
NOBODY HAS DROWNED UNDER THIS HOUSE. IT IS NOT LUCK AND IT IS NOT SKILL EITHER.
